factors.factor: Mismatch between the IPC Template Type definition (21 expected inputs) and the sensor code that supplied only 20 input values. The defect stayed latent because no earlier channel file version used the 21st input, and no check compared the declared and supplied input counts.
factors.evidence: "The definition of the IPC Template Type in the Template Type Definitions file stated that it expected 21 input fields. The sensor code that invoked the Content Interpreter with Channel File 291's Template Instances supplied only 20 input values to match against."

factors.factor: Testing did not exercise the code path that failed: the automated test set used a static channel file with wildcard matching in the 21st field, so the non-wildcard comparison against the 21st input was never tested.
factors.evidence: "a static set of 12 test cases was selected. A channel file was defined manually for use within these test cases, and it used a regex wildcard matching criterion in the 21st field for all Template Instances." | "The IPC Template Type was stress tested with a test Template Instance in a test environment consisting of a variety of operating systems and workloads. It passed the stress test and was validated for use."

factors.factor: The Content Validator checked channel files against the 21-input definition rather than against the inputs the sensor actually supplies, so it passed content that would crash the sensor.
factors.evidence: "The Content Validator evaluated the new Template Instances. It based its assessment on the expectation that the IPC Template Type would be provided with 21 inputs."

factors.factor: Memory-safety weakness in the kernel driver: the code read the input at index 0x14 without a bounds check, so a malformed count produced an invalid memory read in kernel space rather than a graceful rejection.
factors.evidence: "The code read the input at index 0x14 (the 21st element), which did not point to valid memory. The code performed a NULL pointer check, then read through the invalid pointer, resulting in the out-of-bounds read and the bugcheck."

factors.factor: Kernel-mode placement of a driver that evaluates externally delivered content amplified the impact, since a fault crashes the whole system and boot-time loading can prevent recovery without manual intervention.
factors.evidence: "The Falcon sensor uses a kernel driver (csagent.sys), loaded from an early phase of system boot so the sensor can observe and defend against malware that launches before user mode processes start."

action_items.action: Make the Content Validator check each channel file against the input count the sensor code actually supplies at runtime, and reject content that references inputs beyond that count, rather than validating only against the Template Type Definitions file.

Add bounds checking in csagent.sys before reading any input index in the Content Interpreter, so that out-of-range or missing inputs produce a graceful rejection or non-match instead of an invalid kernel memory read.

Reconcile the IPC Template Type definition with the sensor's input-supply code so that the declared input count and the supplied input count are generated from a single source of truth and cross-checked in CI.

Extend test coverage for Template Types so that the test corpus must exercise every input field the Template Type declares, with both wildcard and non-wildcard matching criteria for each field, and add a CI check that fails when any declared input is not covered.
action_items.owner_role: Sensor QA and test engineering team

action_items.action: Evaluate moving Rapid Response Content evaluation out of kernel mode, or isolating its interpreter in a user-mode component, so that faults in externally delivered content cannot crash the whole system. Deliver a written design decision with a go/no-go recommendation.
